To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

requirements are shaped in the project by filtering the understanding of requirements through preconceptions, shifting the understanding of requirements to fit the project participants’ expectations, and negotiating the understanding of requirements between project participants.

“Requirement shaping in software development projects is a process where attitudes, preconceptions, and expectations about the system are repeatedly filtered, shifted and nego- tiated among project participants.”
the understanding of requirements is filtered, negotiated and shifted in the process of software requirement engineering.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the interpretation of requirements is shaped during the development project.

how requirements are understood and shaped by different parties during a software development project, how this shaping is influenced by the participants’ preconceptions, expectations and attitudes, and how the shaping affects the outcome of the project.
how requirements are shaped in a project.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the requirements of the system, which was developed, were filtered, negotiated and shifted in the understanding of the project participants, and this process was influenced by their technology frames.
The filtering, negotiating and shifting processes are not the only ones that take place during a project.

the filtering, negotiation and shifts in the understanding of IS requirements are a part of an ongoing process that takes place during the whole life-cycle of the project, and that these processes have an effect on the final outcome of the project.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
requirements engineering should be seen as a process where the interpretation of the requirements is negotiated between project participants.
requirements engineering is not a linear process, and the understanding of requirements is not a one-to-one correspondence between the system and its environment, but rather a complex social process.
the understanding of requirements is shaped by filtering, shifting and negotiating of the requirements.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the interpretation and understanding of requirements is not a static process, but rather a process where attitudes, expectations and preconceptions are filtered, shifted, and negotiated.

the understanding of software requirements is a social process that involves the filtering of attitudes and expectations of different parties, the shifting of these expectations and attitudes, and the negotiation between different parties.
the requirement shaping process should be taken into account in requirement management.
